blocks.text: The DLP Operational page provides a clear and concise summary of the system's performance, stability, and utilization.
The DLP Operational page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Track key metrics, identify problems, and verify that Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) aligns with operational goals.
Gain insights into the health of the endpoint, thereby ensuring that the system functions properly and as designed to avoid sensitive data leakage.

blocks.text: On the DLP Operational page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > DLP Operational) you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the data in the page by OS, Last Connected, Endpoint DLP Version, Endpoint DLP Version, Endpoint Device Control Policy Version, and Zscaler Client Connector Version.
Export: Click the Export icon to download the Endpoint DLP Operational Report in a CSV or PDF format.

Total Endpoints: Indicates the total number of endpoint devices (Windows and macOS) on which Endpoint DLP is installed. Click the numeric value under Windows and macOS to view the endpoint details on the Device Investigation page.
Users in Exemption Mode: Indicates the total number of users in exemption mode.

Endpoint Connectivity Status for Last 30 Days: View the connectivity status of the endpoints in your organization for the last 30 days in the form of a pie chart. You can set the time frame to define the active status of the endpoint. The available options are Last 3 Days, Last 7 Days, or Last 14 Days. Click anywhere in the pie chart to view details corresponding to the endpoint on the Device Investigation page.
Action Items: View possible action to be taken based on the endpoint data that is collected. The possible cause and the action are:

Number of Endpoints On Which Anti-Tampering is Disabled <X>: Disabling anti-tampering can expose your security settings, making your system vulnerable to unauthorized modifications. Zscaler recommends enabling anti-tampering to ensure system integrity. To learn more about how to enable anti-tampering, see Anti-Tampering for Zscaler Client Connector.

Over <X>% of Users Are in Exemption Mode: A high number of users in exemption mode indicates misuse or potential abuse, resulting in security threats. Review your exemption policies to ensure appropriate usage.

Number of Endpoints That Are Offline For Over Two Weeks - <X>: Endpoints that are offline for over two weeks might impact security monitoring and data protection. Consider investigating these devices. You are redirected to the Device Investigation page when you click the Click here to view the offline devices link.

Scanning HDD Drives Is Disabled: Disabling HDD drives scanning might prevent visibility into sensitive data stored on these endpoints. Enable this setting to enhance security coverage. You can enable the HDD drive scanning from Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Configuration. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan, Endpoint Settings, and Channels.

Endpoint Data Scan Report Is Disabled: Disabling Endpoint Data Scan reporting might prevent visibility into sensitive data stored on the endpoints. Enable this setting to enhance security coverage. You can enable reporting for Endpoint Data Scan from Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Configuration. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan, Endpoint Settings, and Channels.

Number of macOS Endpoints with Full Disk Access Disabled: Full Disk Access is disabled on macOS endpoints, which prevents Endpoint DLP from functioning properly and reduces protection coverage. Configure a Mobile Device Management (MDM) profile to enforce Full Disk Access. To learn more, see About Device Investigation.

Policy Version: Indicates the percentage of endpoints that are using the latest policy versions of both Endpoint DLP and Device Control policies. While calculating the percentage, both the Endpoint DLP policy version and Device Control policy versions are considered. An endpoint is considered to be using the latest version of the policy if both the Endpoint DLP policy version and Device Control policy versions are the latest, else it is considered to be using the earlier version. Click View All; a drawer appears, and it shows the policy version breakdown for Endpoint DLP and Device Control policy versions on the endpoints.

Endpoint DLP Version: Indicates the percentage of endpoints using the latest or earlier endpoint DLP version. The current Endpoint DLP versions of the Windows and macOS endpoints are shown. Click View All; a drawer appears, and it shows the Endpoint DLP version breakdown for Windows and macOS. Click the numeric values in the endpoints column to view the endpoint details on the Device Investigation page.
